questions.question: What annotation exposes an Apex class as a custom REST endpoint?
options: @AuraEnabled
@RestResource(urlMapping='/...')
@InvocableMethod
@future(callout=true)
questions.explanation: @RestResource with a urlMapping makes an Apex class reachable at /services/apexrest/<mapping>.

questions.question: Why return real HTTP status codes (201, 400, 404, 500) from an Apex REST method instead of always returning 200?
options: Salesforce requires exactly one status code per org
Status codes have no effect, they're purely cosmetic
So callers can handle success/failure programmatically using standard HTTP semantics
200 is the only status code Apex REST supports
questions.explanation: Meaningful status codes let any HTTP client branch on outcome without parsing response text — it's the whole point of using HTTP semantics.

questions.question: What's the risk of a "global without sharing" Apex REST class with no explicit CRUD/FLS checks?
options: It will fail to compile
It can let an under-permissioned caller read or write data they shouldn't have access to
It automatically throws an exception on every request
There is no risk as long as the endpoint uses HTTPS
questions.explanation: "without sharing" plus no CRUD/FLS checks means your code — not the platform — is the only thing standing between the caller and the data.

questions.question: When would you build a custom Apex REST endpoint instead of using the standard Salesforce REST API?
options: Always — Apex REST should be the default for every integration
Never — the standard REST API covers every possible use case
Only when the external system requires SOAP/WSDL
When you need custom validation, multi-object transactions, or a payload shape the standard API can't produce
questions.explanation: Apex REST is for cases the standard API genuinely can't cover; reaching for it by default adds unnecessary code to maintain and test.

questions.question: In Apex SOAP web services, what does Salesforce auto-generate for the consuming system?
options: A Named Credential
A WSDL describing the available operations
A Platform Event definition
An External Service OpenAPI spec
questions.explanation: Global classes with webservice methods produce a WSDL that the SOAP client uses to know what operations exist and how to call them.
